message: No detected untrusted source handling: The code pulls data via `dvc pull` and loads pickle files directly without any checksum verification, signature validation, or pinned revision check.
No detected label flipping detection: No code checks label distributions, validates label values against an expected set, or uses any label-noise detection tool before or during training.
No detected data poisoning defenses: No outlier detection, statistical anomaly checks, or filtering of suspicious inputs is performed anywhere in the data preparation pipeline.
No detected model integrity verification: The code loads pickle files directly with no hash check, signature verification, or pinned revision before deserializing the model, encoder, or binarizer.
No detected label distribution validation: No code checks class balance, label distribution, or expected label set before or during training; train_model simply calls model.fit directly.
No detected backdoor or trigger detection: There is no trigger detection, activation analysis, or gradient anomaly detection anywhere in the training pipeline.
No detected differential privacy: The code uses a standard CatBoostClassifier with no differential privacy library or DP-SGD mechanism applied.
No detected adversarial robustness testing: No adversarial robustness testing libraries (Foolbox, ART, FGSM, PGD) or stress tests are present anywhere in the code.

No detected metric tampering protection: There is no isolation of a held-out test set from training data, no hashing/signing of evaluation data, and while multiple metrics (precision, recall, fbeta) are computed, there are no controls preventing metric manipulation.
No detected output bounds checks: The prediction result is used directly after model.predict() with no NaN checks, probability bounds validation, or any other output sanity checks.
No detected prompt injection defenses: This is a tabular classification model (CatBoostClassifier), not an LLM, so prompt injection defenses are not applicable and none are implemented.
